messages:
Priya: quick UX thread on trace viewer exports and stack trace folding. thinking about two things: where to surface correlation-id copy and how export formats should be discovered. cc: @Noah for copy, @Connor for a11y.

Noah: For copy: show the correlation id as a button with a visible copy icon and text fallback on hover. Label it with the full context, e.g. "Correlation ID: 123abc (copy)" so assistive tech reads purpose.

Connor: Accessibility rules: avoid putting copy inside a tooltip-only UI. Tooltips are not announced by SRs by default. Make sure the copy control is focusable and has `aria-live` feedback when copied.

Priya: Agree. UX question: should the copy live inline next to the id or be in the kebab menu for each request row? Inline increases clutter but is immediate for debugging flows.

Evelyn: Inline is better for "one-click" workflows. Most SREs want to copy correlation id quick and paste into log search. We can hide the text label on small screens but keep button visible.

Noah: Copy microcopy: instead of "Copied" use "Correlation ID copied to clipboard" so context is explicit. Also show a small transient inline toast anchored to the ID, not center-screen.

Connor: Keyboard: `Tab` should move: request row -> correlation copy -> expand row -> kebab. Focus order matters here. Current mock has kebab before copy which is confusing.

Priya: Good catch. We'll reorder in the DOM to match that. Another export question: users want both quick JSON export and richer downloads (HAR + plain events CSV). Two approaches: quick-export icon + dropdown formats, or keep quick JSON only and surface other formats in kebab. Thoughts?

Evelyn: Prefer quick JSON for trace, and put HAR/CSV under kebab. Many tools expect JSON for traces; HAR is more niche. But show a subtle "More formats" affordance so users know there are options.

Noah: Copy/correlate naming: in the kebab menu show "Export as JSON (trace)" and "Export as HAR (network)". Use parentheses to provide context for screenreaders.

Connor: A11y enforcement: Export actions should announce file type and suggested filename via SR: e.g. "Downloading Trace-<id>.json". Also provide a `role=status` element for progressive feedback.

Priya: On stack traces: should frames be collapsed by default with a "Show n more frames" affordance? Designers worry this hides important info. Engineers worry about noise.

Evelyn: Collapse by default for frames from vendor libraries, expand for application frames. We can auto-detect via package path heuristics. Show a clear explainer label: "3 library frames collapsed (expand)".

Noah: Copy text for collapsed section: "Collapsed frames are from third-party libraries. Expand to see full stacktrace." Keep it short.

Connor: Keyboard for expand/collapse: `Enter` or `Space` to toggle when focused, and move focus into the first revealed frame after expand. On collapse, return focus to the toggle.

Priya: UX small: add a permalink icon next to each frame to deep-link into logs or the request detail view. That link should open in new tab and have `rel=noopener`.

Evelyn: Also propose a small inline timeline scrubber in the trace header that shows error hotspots; clicking hotspot jumps to the frame/time and highlights corresponding log lines. That would reduce manual hunting.

Noah: Copy for export CTA in header: "Quick export (JSON) \u2014 Shift+E" show shortcut in tooltip and in kebab menu label. People rely on keyboard.

Connor: I'll run a quick AT check on the mock once updated. Also check contrast tokens for the permalink and quick-export icons; some tokens are failing 4.5:1 on hover.

Priya: Action items: 1) Move correlation copy inline and fix focus order; 2) Add quick-export JSON button in header with Shift+E shortcut; 3) Put HAR/CSV and advanced export in kebab; 4) Collapse vendor frames by default with accessible toggle; 5) Add timeline hotspots that map to stack frames.

Evelyn: I'll produce updated mocks for desktop + mobile showing collapsed frames and inline copy.

Noah: I'll draft the microcopy strings and keyboard shortcut help text.

Connor: I'll add the a11y acceptance criteria and run a short screenreader walkthrough once mocks are ready.

QA-Bot: Reminder: add an automated e2e that copies correlation id and asserts aria-live message and file download name for export.

DeployBot: Staging deploy scheduled 2026-04-01T07:00:00Z for trace UX experiment.

Priya: thanks all — please drop links to mocks here when ready and I'll pick final variant for the sprint.
